title: Measure of set coherence
authors: Jiabo Panel, Yu Guo, Yuqin Wang
abstract: Set coherence is a quantum resource for a set of states that characterizes whether a collection of quantum states contains coherence, namely whether these states fail to be simultaneously incoherent in a common basis. In this work, we show that the free operations of set coherence are common commutativity-preserving quantum channels, from which we then establish an axiomatic framework for set-coherence measure (SCM). Within this framework, we investigate the robustness based measures deduced by taking, respectively, the average, maximum, and sum of the single-state robustnesses over a common reference basis, where the first two were previously introduced in the literature and we check here whether they satisfy our SCM axioms. Consequently, we show that the averaged robustness is an SCM but it is neither unified nor complete, the maximal robustness is a unified SCM but is neither complete nor strongly superadditive, whereas the sum robustness is a complete SCM. Furthermore, we propose several classes of SCMs based on pairwise commutators. We show that the Schatten $p$-norm based SCMs are complete and strongly superadditive. We also find that the universal fourth-order Bargmann gap measure proposed in the literature is a complete and strongly superadditive quantifier of set coherence. Finally, we discuss the operational meaning of the SCM in the context of optimal approximate quantum broadcasting, and show that the amount of set coherence can closely reflect the performance of this task.
summary: This work introduces a resource theory for 'set coherence,' a measure quantifying how far a set of quantum states is from being simultaneously diagonalizable. By establishing an axiomatic framework, the authors rigorously test various candidate measures, proving that certain constructions, like the sum robustness, satisfy the necessary mathematical criteria for a robust quantifier.
main_problem: The paper develops a systematic resource theory for 'set coherence,' quantifying whether a collection of quantum states fails to be simultaneously incoherent in a common basis.
main_result: It establishes an axiomatic framework for Set-Coherence Measures (SCMs) and compares various robustness-based quantifiers, finding that the sum robustness and Schatten p-norm based measures are complete and strongly superadditive.
method: The authors use axiomatic definitions derived from the free operations of set coherence (which are common commutativity-preserving quantum channels) to categorize and test candidate coherence measures.
model_or_system: The study analyzes sets of quantum states, $\vec{ho} = \{ho_j\}$, acting on a Hilbert space $H$. It relates set coherence to the ability to perfectly broadcast the set of states, drawing parallels to single-state coherence measures.
key_observables: Set coherence, various robustness measures ($C'_R, C''_R$), and the performance of approximate quantum broadcasting.
important_parameters: The dimension of the Hilbert space ($d \ge 2$), and the structure of the set of states $\vec{ho}$.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that the free operations of set coherence are common commutativity-preserving quantum channels, leading to the axiomatic definition of SCMs.
paper_structure: The paper first defines set coherence and establishes the axiomatic framework for SCMs. It then investigates and compares several robustness-based measures (average, maximum, sum) against these axioms. Finally, it proposes and analyzes specific classes of SCMs, including those based on Schatten norms and the Bargmann gap.
why_interesting: The development of a resource theory for set coherence provides a powerful, generalized tool for quantifying non-classical correlations in multi-state systems, which is crucial for understanding tasks like quantum broadcasting.
